Bahrain Private-Sector Pension Calculator

Enter your age when your service ends, your contribution period and your average monthly wage over the last five years to see your pension or lump sum and your monthly contributions.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Calculate your pension

The contributory wage shown on your SIO statement. Capped at BD 4,000.

Private-sector pension conditions in Bahrain

CaseConditionEntitlement
Old-age pensionService ends at 60, with at least 180 months of contributions2% × years of contribution × average wage of the last 5 years
Early retirementBefore 60, with at least 240 monthsThe same pension reduced by age (20%, 15% or 10%)
Lump sumReaching 60 with fewer than 180 months15% × average wage × months of contribution
Less than one year—Refund of the employee's own contributions only

Examples:
Retiring at 60 after 30 years on an average of BD 1,200: 1,200 × 30 ÷ 50 = BD 720 a month (60%).
Early retirement at 52 after 25 years on an average of BD 1,000: BD 500 before the reduction, BD 450 after 10%.
Reaching 60 after 10 years (120 months) on an average of BD 800: a lump sum of 0.15 × 800 × 120 = BD 14,400.

What changed in 2022

  • The pension became 2% per year (1/50) instead of 1/60 in the original text, calculated on a five-year average instead of two years.
  • Women's retirement age became 60, like men's, and the contribution period rose to 180 months at 60 and 240 months for early retirement.
  • The automatic annual pension increase stopped; increases are now by ministerial decision.
  • The employer's share rises gradually to 17% in 2028, and the employee's share to 7%.

This calculator is for Bahrainis in the private sector. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

When is a Bahraini in the private sector entitled to a pension?

When service ends on reaching 60, for men and women, with at least 180 months of contributions. Early retirement before 60 is allowed with 240 months, with a reduction set by age. The 2022 reform replaced age 55 with 60 for women.

How is the pension calculated in Bahrain?

One fiftieth (2%) of the average monthly contributory wage over the last five years, multiplied by the years of contribution. 30 years on an average of BD 1,200 gives 1,200 × 30 ÷ 50 = BD 720, or 60% of the average. Specialist sources give a cap of 80%.

How much is the early retirement reduction?

Table 1 attached to the law sets it by age at the time of the claim. Law firms publish it as 20% under 45, 15% from 45 to 49 and 10% from 50 to under 60. The calculator applies these rates as an estimate until the official table is published.

What if I have fewer than 180 months at 60?

You receive a lump sum of 15% of the average monthly wage of the last five years for each month of contribution, about 1.8 months' wages per year (Article 43). With less than one full year, only your own contributions are refunded.

Does the pension increase every year?

The 2022 reform ended the automatic 3% annual increase; any increase is now by ministerial decision after board approval. One-off 3% increases were paid for 2021 and 2022, capped at BD 30 each. A bill to restore annual increases passed the Council of Representatives in November 2025 but was not in force as of October 2026.

What are the social insurance contributions in Bahrain?

For the pension branch: 7% from the employee, and 15% from the employer in 2026, rising by 1% a year to 17% in 2028. Contributions apply to wages up to BD 4,000 a month according to specialist sources.
